name: "Kung Pao" Cauliflower-Edamame Lettuce Cups with Cashews & Spicy Mayo

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ medium heads cauliflower
3 red bell peppers
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root
1 ½ heads butter (Boston) lettuce

instructions.primary_message: Separate each cauliflower into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces; divide between two baking sheet pans.
Trim, seed, and large dice bell peppers; add to the baking sheets with the cauliflower.
Add edamame to the baking sheets. Drizzle veggies with oil and season with salt; toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 cups edamame
3 tbsp toasted sesame oil
¾ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Place baking sheets in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until veggies are tender, 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic; place both in a small saucepan.
Add water, soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, chili-garlic sauce, cornstarch, and additional oil to the saucepan with the ginger and garlic; whisk to combine the sauce.
instructions.secondary_message:
¾ cup water
⅓ cup soy sauce
3 tbsp brown sugar
3 tbsp rice vinegar
1 ½ tbsp chili-garlic sauce
1 ½ tbsp cornstarch
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil

instructions.primary_message: Bring sauce to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium and simmer, whisking frequently, until sauce is thickened and glossy, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, place mayo and chili-garlic sauce in a small bowl; whisk to combine the spicy mayo and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ cup mayonnaise
1 ½ tbsp chili-garlic sauce

instructions.primary_message: When the veggies are done, drizzle with the sauce, and stir to combine.
To serve, separate the lettuce into leaves. Pile leaves, in stacks of two per wrap, onto plates; fill each wrap with veggies. Top with cashews and spicy mayo. Enjoy!
